title: Repo market networks: dynamics under financial stress
summary: This ECB Working Paper examines the resilience of the euro-denominated repo market during episodes of financial stress using transaction-level data and network analysis from 2021 to mid-February 2025. The paper finds that the institutional repo network exhibits a core-periphery structure with connectivity intensifying during stress periods, while trading volumes and repo spreads remain broadly stable at the sectoral level. Notably, the euro repo market as a whole displays lower spreads during periods of elevated financial stress, indicating the market functions as a shock absorber rather than a source of contagion. [Disclaimer: Views expressed are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect official ECB positions.]
key_points: The euro repo market displays a core-periphery network structure with a small core of highly active institutions conducting most trading alongside a larger group of less active participants
Connectivity between institutions, especially banks trading with other banks, has grown over time even during periods of stress
Trading volumes and borrowing costs between different types of institutions remain stable under stress
At the market level, borrowing costs decline as financial stress increases, indicating the repo market helps absorb shocks through pricing adjustments
The analysis uses data from the Securities Financing Transactions Data Store (SFTDS) covering 2021 to mid-February 2025
Financial stress is measured using the Composite indicator of systemic stress (CISS)
why_it_matters: Understanding how the euro repo market functions during stress is critical for financial stability policymakers. The repo market is the largest segment of euro money markets, accounting for 56% of daily transactions and 30% of outstanding amounts. This research provides empirical evidence that the euro repo market maintains resilience during stress episodes, with the network structure and pricing mechanisms helping to absorb shocks rather than amplify them. The findings have implications for designing repo market regulations and financial stability frameworks. [Note: Author's personal research, not official ECB position.]
market_structure_context: The paper provides detailed analysis of repo market network dynamics including core-periphery structure, network density and strength metrics, and how these change during stress periods. It examines transaction-level data mapping repo activity between counterparties, covering trading volumes, spreads, haircuts, and maturities. The findings show intensified connectivity during stress periods with stable sectoral-level trading volumes and spreads, indicating robust market plumbing.
